title: Acute abdominal pain
candidateBrief: You are a junior doctor in the surgical assessment unit. Liam O'Brien, 19, has come in with abdominal pain since yesterday. Take a focused history. You may use the Examine and Investigations panels. You will be asked questions afterwards.

patient.name: Liam O'Brien
patient.setting: Surgical assessment unit, lying still on the bed.
patient.openingStatement: I've got this really bad pain in my stomach, it's been getting worse since yesterday.
patient.demeanour: Lying very still, winces when he moves or coughs, a bit embarrassed to be making a fuss.
patient.speechStyle: Casual, young, uses words like 'tummy', 'properly bad', 'dunno'.

ice.ideas: Thinks it might be a dodgy kebab.
ice.concerns: Worried he'll miss his exams next week.
ice.expectations: Wants painkillers and to go home.

freelyShared: The pain started yesterday evening around his belly button.
Now it's mostly low down on the right side.
It's a constant sharp pain now; walking, coughing and bumps in the car make it much worse.

revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I've been sick twice and I don't want to eat anything, which isn't like me.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: fever or feeling hot and cold
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: I felt a bit hot and shivery last night.
Haven't been since yesterday morning. That was normal.
No, nothing like that down there.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: past medical history, operations, medications or allergies
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: Never been in hospital. I took some paracetamol. I'm allergic to penicillin — I got a rash as a kid.

revealOnlyIfAsked.trigger: when he last ate or drank
revealOnlyIfAsked.answer: Just some water this morning. Last proper food was lunch yesterday.

patient.cue: It really hurts when I move. Is that normal for food poisoning?

examFindings.finding: Tender with guarding in the right iliac fossa, maximal at McBurney's point. Rovsing's sign positive. Bowel sounds reduced. No masses.

postEncounterQuestions.q: What is the most likely diagnosis and your differentials?
postEncounterQuestions.modelAnswer: Acute appendicitis. Differentials include mesenteric adenitis, terminal ileitis (Crohn's), renal colic or UTI, testicular torsion, and gastroenteritis.

Nil by mouth, IV access, bloods including group and save, IV fluids, analgesia and antiemetic, IV antibiotics avoiding penicillins given his allergy, surgical review for laparoscopic appendicectomy, consider imaging if diagnosis uncertain.

items.text: Takes a structured pain history including migration of the pain
Asks about nausea, vomiting, appetite and bowels
Asks about testicular pain (or examines testes)
Asks about past history, medications and allergies
Establishes time of last food and drink
Examines the abdomen and checks observations
Addresses his concerns about exams and explains next steps
